title: Data Type
definition: A data type defines a set of values together with the operations and constraints applicable to those values.
purpose: Make valid values and valid operations explicit enough to reason about program behavior.
history: Type systems developed as languages needed systematic ways to classify values and constrain operations.
mental_model: A type is a rulebook for a family of values, not a decorative label attached to spelling.
analogy: A tool category suggests valid uses; the analogy fails because language type rules are formally defined and can vary by language.
common_mistakes: Treating text containing digits as a number
Assuming every language has identical primitive types
industry_notes: Types form part of data contracts across application, API, storage, and analytics boundaries.
ai_notes: AI may choose a syntactically valid but semantically wrong type; require a domain justification.
interview_notes: Ask how type information prevents classes of invalid operations without guaranteeing business correctness.
exercise_candidates: Match domain fields to types and justify exceptions
